answer: Proof-of-space-time resists Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to seal a unique, incompressible dataset to its public key and prove continuous custody against audits from a randomness beacon. Instead of letting fake identities slip through a porous inlet or root like wild juniper in cheap RAM, the protocol enforces verifiable disk reservation and read-I/O costs per identity. However, large storage providers with surplus drive capacity can still fund multiple clones.
